_about: Census-people store for the 2013 federal election, the venue-proxy sibling of the voter-footprint demo lanes in data/booth-seifa-voter-YYYY.json (2016+; the AEC published no 'Votes by SA1' product before 2016, so a 2013 booth cannot be weighted by where its voters live). A booth's demo block is the 2011 Census Basic Community Profile counts of the SA1 its VENUE sits in — the geo key of booth-seifa-2013.json — describing the venue's neighbourhood, never the booth's voters; persons is a real SA1 headcount, never a weighted pseudo-population. A division's row is the exact 2011-census sum over the SA1s of its CED-2011 membership (the boundary set the 2013 election ran on; ABS Mcewen/Mcmillan/Mcpherson spellings normalised), not an average of its booth rows. Shares mirror the GCP lanes: age renormalised over the 11 B01 bands (no age-not-stated column); language other-at-home over English-only + other; overseas-born over country-of-birth stated, and the curated birthplace-country (cob) shares riding that same country-stated basis — the 2011 B09 prints no England or Scotland subsets (it merges the UK into one row), so the GCP-era ten-country set is trimmed to eight here (country order in cobKeys); university (bachelor and above) per the aged-15+ population less level-of-education-not-stated; blue-collar (technicians/trades + machinery operators/drivers + labourers of B45B the ANZSCO occupation major groups) over the eight stated occupation groups, inadequately-described and not-stated occupations out of the frame. Income lanes mirror the voter stores on the BCP's own tables: B28 households by the 14-band weekly household-income grid are re-weighted to ADULTS at the data/income-dist.json factors (each band's family share from B26's family-income Tot over its family-composition mix in the SA1 — national mix as fallback — the rest non-family at the national mean; household mass rides the Tot columns, never the B28 fam/non columns, small-SA1 perturbation independently shaving the splits; partial-stated and all-not-stated households sit outside the basis). loinc is the adult share below the national 25th-percentile weekly household-income cut the store-level incomeCuts record carries (the BCP national adults histogram's cut band split linearly, in 2011 dollars), hiinc the adult share in the $4,000-and-top band, incMed the band-interpolated median weekly household income in 2011 dollars on the HOUSEHOLD basis (ABS's own published-median basis — the adults-weighted histogram would read a few hundred dollars higher, skewed by couples). The national row pools the division sums. A booth whose venue SA1 records no residents (commercial/industrial blocks; counts.boothsGeoEmpty) carries demo:null, as does one whose geo key is absent from the BCP (counts.boothsGeoMissing); inside a present block a lane is nulled rather than clamped when the BCP's small-area perturbation would put its share outside [0,1] (counts.boothsGeo-carrying rows only). Booth records carry geo of data/booth-seifa-2013.json; its venue-proxy caveats apply here too. The demoI blocks interpolate the people figures between the 2011 and 2016 censuses to election day (day-share 0.415982 of the intercensal span — the SEIFA pcti lanes' own factors, asserted identical to data/booth-seifa-2013.json's _pcti record): each demoI lane blends the two census sides' shares, a lane missing on either side falling back to the measured block for that lane; incMed and the incomeCutsI dollar figures come from the 2011 census side alone, never a mixed-currency blend. The far side of the blend is data/booth-demo-2013-c1.json. deliveryBasis: venue-proxy per booth (SA1 of the premises); exact CED-2011 census sum per division

booths.booth: Perth East Interstate Polling Centre PPVC

demoInterp.nullRule: a booth missing its demo block on either census side, or a lane missing on either side, shows the measured figure instead
